templates.name: Algebrite
templates.description: Computer algebra in the browser: learners run and edit CAS code (simplify, differentiate, integrate, solve, matrices, units, plots), and quizzes accept any mathematically equivalent answer such as 1/2, 0,5, 50% or \frac{1}{2}.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: actively maintained, bundled (dist/index.js, no external CDN), very thorough README with a CAS tutorial and quiz checks with tolerances and units. Pinned to tag 0.7.1 (= master HEAD, the version the README documents); the semantically higher tag 6.0.0 is an older commit (Feb 2026) and was ignored.

templates.name: DuckDB
templates.description: DuckDB in the browser for SQL and data analysis: executable query blocks and an interactive terminal; queries can read CSV, JSON and Parquet files from URLs.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: maintained, versioned, detailed README; strong for data analysis with real data files.

templates.name: JSXGraph
templates.description: Interactive geometry constructions, function plots and dynamic mathematical visualizations from JSXGraph code; learners can drag points and sliders, or edit and rerun the code themselves.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: released (0.0.3 = current default branch), README with worked examples for every macro, JSXGraph bundled in the repo's dist/index.js. Loads MathJax 3 from jsDelivr for formulas; still a 0.0.x version.

templates.name: PGlite
templates.description: PostgreSQL in the browser via PGlite: executable SQL blocks and an interactive terminal, each on a named, separate database.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: maintained, versioned, very detailed README; real PostgreSQL in the browser.

templates.name: PixiJS Stories
templates.description: Write interactive, branching picture stories line by line like a screenplay – backgrounds, characters, dialog, choices, point-and-click, effects, sound and read-aloud – and check reached endings or variables in quizzes; learners can also edit and rerun stories. No JavaScript needed, but PixiJS is available for own animations and games.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: extensive README with live examples, builtin characters and backgrounds, accessibility and language options, tests, MIT license; PixiJS is bundled in dist/index.js (no external CDN). Tag 0.5.2 (= HEAD); very young project (created Oct 2026, 8 releases in two weeks), so pin the version.

templates.name: Pyodide
templates.description: Full CPython in the browser via Pyodide: editable Python blocks with output, or fixed code that shows only its result, including matplotlib plots.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: maintained, many releases, full CPython with scientific packages. Caveat: loads Pyodide (several MB) from the jsDelivr CDN on first use, so slow connections wait noticeably.

templates.name: ScratchBlocks
templates.description: Real Scratch 3 blocks and stage in LiaScript code blocks, with grade-level profiles and automatically checked tasks.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: maintained, several releases, bundled, real Scratch 3 look with checked tasks — the closest match to what children know from Scratch.

templates.name: Skulpt
templates.description: Executable Python blocks run by the Skulpt interpreter in the browser, with turtle graphics drawn on a canvas.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: maintained and versioned, everything bundled in the repository (no external CDN), clear examples. The turtle mode (@Skulpt.eval(skulpt_canvas) with a canvas element) suits younger learners; @Skulpt.terminal opens a Python REPL, @Skulpt.runProject runs multi-file projects.

templates.name: three.js
templates.description: Interactive 3D scenes with three.js: describe buildings line by line without programming (houses, roofs, walls, domes, towers, trees) and explore them in 3D, as floor plan or section, write plain three.js JavaScript, or load glTF models.
templates.note: Rating 5/5: versioned (0.1.0, Oct 2026), thorough README with a command reference and many examples (houses, walls, a mosque, animations), three.js bundled in the repo (dist/index.js). The .building variants need no programming; @THREE.scene and @THREE.scene.building hide the code and show only the view; @[THREE.gltf](url) loads a model from an external URL. First release, so watch for changes in later versions.

templates.name: ABCjs
templates.description: Write music in ABC notation and show it as rendered sheet music with playback; with @ABCJS.eval learners edit the notation and hear the result, including tablature, instrument and tempo options.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: clear README with examples for all four macros and an options table, strong value for music lessons. Pinned to release 0.0.2 (2022), which loads its bundle from jsDelivr; main has a few later commits (undocumented staffwidth option, polyfill for old browsers). Audio playback loads instrument samples from paulrosen.github.io (external, needs internet).

templates.name: AVR8js
templates.description: Simulates an Arduino Uno in the browser: learners edit and run Arduino sketches (single or multi-file) or AVR assembly and see the effect on virtual parts like LEDs, buttons, sensors, displays and servos, with serial I/O and sliders to change sensor values.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: actively maintained (release 0.4.0, Sept 2026), extensive README with many hardware examples. Sketches are compiled on the external Wokwi build service (hexi.wokwi.com), so running code needs internet access and sends the code there; the simulator itself runs locally from dist/index.js.

templates.name: BeforeAndAfter
templates.description: Compare two images in one frame with a slider that reveals the before or the after picture, e.g. a glacier in 1883 and 2015 or two telescope images of the same object.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: simple, self-contained (only its own style.css, no external CDN) and clearly documented, but a single small release (0.0.1, 2024) with a narrow purpose. Usage: @beforeAndAfter(before.jpg,after.jpg) without spaces between the two URLs; image width can be limited with a style comment.

templates.name: Blockly for Python
templates.description: Learners edit Python programs either as Blockly blocks or as text, with both views kept in sync; paired with a Pyodide code block they can run what they built, and quizzes can grade the current code.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: clear README with live examples (options, quiz grading via window.__liaBlockly.getCode, runner pairing with @Pyodide.eval); strong bridge from block to text programming. Pinned to commit (no tag/release, single author, last push 2026-08); the bundle loads BlockMirror from jsDelivr @master and Blockly 10.4.3 from unpkg, and the header imports the Pyodide template from its master branch, so it needs internet and is not fully reproducible.

templates.name: BlocklyCode
templates.description: Blockly blocks over Python and JavaScript code blocks, synchronized in both directions, with turtle graphics, grade-level profiles and checked tasks.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: well documented, bundled, strong for beginners. Young project with a single release so far.

templates.name: Board Mode
templates.description: Optimizes a course for presenting in class: near full-width layout, a font-size slider, content shown only in one view mode, presenter-remote support with black screen, horizontal quizzes, hidden author notes and an @autoscrolling switch.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: very practical for teachers presenting on a board, documented with examples; most features work on import or via HTML attributes (data-lia-only, <!-- horizontal-quiz -->, §:- … -:§), only @autoscrolling is a macro. Pinned to commit (main is 24 commits and README version 0.0.3 ahead of the only tag 0.0.1); changes very frequently, no license file, includes a shim specific to LiaScript 2.5.0.

templates.name: Canvas OCR
templates.description: Adds a drawing canvas with handwriting-to-LaTeX recognition: @canvas fills an existing answer field from handwriting, and @BerechneOCR creates a quiz where learners write a complete multi-line calculation (written arithmetic, equations, derivatives, curve tasks) that is checked step by step.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: very active (Sept 2026) with tests and detailed docs, but pinned to a commit: the only release 0.0.1 contains just @canvas. On first use it downloads the FormulaNet OCR model (~80 MiB) from Hugging Face and transformers.js from jsDelivr/esm.sh; recognition then runs in the browser. Needs Algebrite (the header imports LiaTemplates/algebrite@0.6.3; the README also lists it as an import). Parts of the README and the task options (aufgabe=…) are German; UI texts for languages other than German/English are translated via the external MyMemory API.

templates.name: Chat Simulation
templates.description: Shows a scripted conversation between several people as a messenger-style chat; each message can contain Markdown and LiaScript elements, useful for dialogues, role plays and scenarios.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: clear README with examples and no external libraries; narrow use and only one release (0.0.1, identical to main). The chat is written as a JSON list of {name, message} objects, which needs some care from authors; the typing indicator GIF is loaded from media.tenor.com.

templates.name: ChemmacrosJS
templates.description: Chemical formulas, reaction equations, GHS hazard pictograms and H/P statements in the text, with a syntax like the LaTeX package chemmacros.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: focused and useful for chemistry texts, bundled. No release tag (pinned to a commit), single maintainer. The demo shows the macro syntax as code only; the macros render once the template is imported.

templates.name: Citations
templates.description: Renders inline citations and full bibliography entries from inline BibTeX, a DOI or a remote .bib file in Harvard, APA, Vancouver or IEEE style, so course texts can cite sources properly.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: maintained (2026), tagged releases and a clear README with live examples for every macro; narrow use case. Citation.js is bundled in dist/index.js, but DOI lookups and @bibliography.link fetch data online; @ref and @bibliography.global need window.bibliographyLoad(url) in the course's own @onload.

templates.name: Collaborative Drawing
templates.description: A shared whiteboard for LiaScript classrooms: learners draw lines or place dots on a canvas, optionally over a background image such as a map; the classroom mode decides who sees whose drawing.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: maintained (release 0.1.0, Oct 2026), clear README with tools and a visibility table, no external libraries. Needs LiaScript 2.5.0 or newer (classroom layer API) and `persistent: true` in the course header; synchronisation only works inside a LiaScript classroom. The two commits after 0.1.0 tried and reverted a change for keeping own drawings after a reload (LiaScript stores layers only from course version 1.0.0), so check persistence in your course. Version 0.0.1 is the older pubsub-only variant.

templates.name: Comunica (SPARQL & RDF)
templates.description: Learners write and run SPARQL queries against remote sources or their own RDF data (Turtle, JSON-LD, RDF/XML), convert and draw RDF graphs, try RDFS/OWL reasoning and validate data with SHACL.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: maintained (tag 0.0.5, 2026-10-28), Comunica bundled locally in dist/index.js (~3 MB), README documents all five macros with examples incl. sources, output formats, SPARQL Update, reasoning and SHACL. Narrow topic; queries against remote sources (e.g. DBpedia fragments, Wikidata) depend on those public endpoints, local RDF data works without them.

templates.name: DigiSim
templates.description: Interactive digital logic circuits (gates, buttons, lamps, latches, multiplexers) simulated with DigitalJS; learners toggle inputs and watch signals propagate. Circuits are written as JSON or with a small JavaScript description language (AND, OR, Button, Lamp, wire …).
templates.note: Rating 4/5: strong teaching value for digital logic, README with examples and a JS reference, updated in October 2026 (DigitalJS pinned to 0.14.2, optional manhattan wire routing). Pinned to commit, no release tag; the parser is loaded unversioned from cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/liaTemplates/DigiSim (default branch, minified on the fly), DigitalJS from jsDelivr.

templates.name: Fraction & Formula Quizzes
templates.description: Learners represent fractions by colouring sectors of a circle or cells of a rectangle, fill in input fields placed directly inside formulas, and read tally marks; all are native LiaScript quizzes with checking, hints and solutions.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: clear README with live examples for every macro, bundle (dist/index.js) has no external dependencies, answers can additionally be checked with @Algebrite.check when the Algebrite template is imported. Pinned to commit: main is 6 commits ahead of tag 0.0.2 with the documented formula inputs (\liaquiz in KaTeX), hints and @Strichliste; young project (2026), some README example texts are in German.

templates.name: lia-coordinate
templates.description: Interactive coordinate systems for school mathematics on JSXGraph: points, lines, circles, angles and areas, function plots with zeros and extrema, sliders, value tables, hand-drawn graphs, a set square and compass, and auto-checked construction, perimeter/area and coordinate quizzes.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: very rich and actively maintained (last push Oct 2026), long README with an example per macro; almost every macro also has a German alias (e.g. @Koordinatensystem, @Punkt, @Strecke, @Gerade, @Kreis, @Geodreieck, @Zirkel). Pinned to commit: the only tag (0.0.1) is 70 commits behind and the 0.0.4 the README names does not exist. The header imports LiaTemplates/JSXGraph unversioned from cdn.jsdelivr.net (@main); an optional README.static.md renders static SVG without JSXGraph.

templates.name: Lia-Kachel
templates.description: Makes LiaScript's native drag-and-drop tile quizzes work with touch and pen, and adds order-independent tile sequences, sequences of hidden length that reveal targets step by step, and grouped sequences in table quizzes.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: actively maintained (Oct 2026), bundled and covered by tests; scoring, attempts and feedback stay native LiaScript. No tag exists (the README's recommended 0.7.0 tag is missing), so pinned to commit 7b74fa7; documentation is German only, and a <div class="Kachel"> region enables per-target content checks without a macro.

templates.name: lia-timer
templates.description: Delay the solution and hint buttons of LiaScript quizzes with a countdown, started immediately, after the first check or by a start button, so learners try on their own before they can reveal the answer.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: small, no external CDN (dist/index.js in the repo), clear README with an attribute table and examples. Defines no macros: it works through attributes in the comment above a quiz, e.g. <!-- data-solution-timer="30s" data-solution-timer-start="oncheck" --> or data-hint-timer. Pinned to commit, because the hint timer is newer than the only tag 0.0.1.

templates.name: LiveEdit Embeddings
templates.description: Embeds a code block as an interactive LiaScript LiveEditor (preview, edit or combined view) so learners can change Markdown/LiaScript examples and see the rendered result right away.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: small, clear README with an example per macro, release 0.0.1 equals the current main. Narrow use (teaching Markdown/LiaScript authoring); each block is an iframe of liascript.github.io/LiveEditor with the code Base64-encoded in the URL, so it needs internet and very long examples may hit URL length limits.

templates.name: Mermaid
templates.description: Render Mermaid diagrams (flowcharts, sequence diagrams, user journeys, concept maps …) from text in a code block, or let learners edit the diagram code and redraw it.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: versioned (0.1.4), clear README with inline, code-block and editable examples; useful for any subject that needs diagrams. Last updated 2023; loads mermaid@10.5.0 (pinned) from cdn.jsdelivr.net. @mermaid goes on a ```mermaid code block (or inline with backticks), @mermaid_eval below an editable block.

templates.name: MicroBit-Simulator
templates.description: MicroPython code blocks run in an embedded BBC micro:bit simulator with LED display, buttons and serial output; a variant adds sliders to set sensor values such as light level or temperature.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: released (0.0.1 = current default branch), README with many examples (display, sound, radio, sensors). The simulator is an iframe from python-simulator.usermbit.org (external service, needs internet); the README recommends `persistent: true` in the course header so the simulator survives slide changes.

templates.name: Orthography
templates.description: Orthography exercises: learners correct a sentence or longer text with errors (@orthography, @orthographytext), fill dictation gaps read aloud by the narrator (@diktat), and read line-numbered texts (@linenumbers), with reset, hints and a solution button after a set number of attempts.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: actively maintained (Sept 2026) with tests and a clear README, no external services. Pinned to a commit because release 0.0.1 lacks @orthographytext and @linenumbers. @diktat relies on the course narrator voice (browser TTS) for the read-aloud word.

templates.name: p5.js
templates.description: Runs p5.js sketches from JavaScript code blocks (or a project of several blocks) on a canvas, with a console for live commands – for creative coding, drawing and animation.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: small, tagged and clearly documented with runnable demos; very good for creative coding. Unchanged since 2021 and loads the old p5.js 1.2.0 from cdnjs (still reachable); sketches access p5 functions through the p5. prefix (instance mode).

templates.name: PlantUML
templates.description: Renders PlantUML text as diagrams (UML class, sequence, activity, state and more) as SVG or PNG, either fixed or in an editable block learners can change and redraw.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: release 0.0.11 (2024), short but clear README. Diagram source is compressed into a URL and rendered by the public plantuml.com server (script from cdn-0.plantuml.com), so it needs internet access and diagram content leaves the browser; no offline use.

templates.name: PouchDB
templates.description: Run a NoSQL document database (PouchDB) in the browser: learners write JavaScript to store documents, run MongoDB-style Mango queries, geospatial queries and attachments, or work in an interactive database terminal.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: extensive README (CRUD, bulk, indexes, query operators, geo queries, changes, attachments, best practices), PouchDB 9 and plugins bundled in the repo (dist/index.js, no external CDN), in-memory storage. Single release 0.0.1 (Oct 2025); queries are written in JavaScript, and examples should end with db.destroy() as the README advises.

templates.name: Redis
templates.description: Experiment with Redis key-value operations (strings, hashes, lists, sets, TTL, transactions, Lua scripts) entirely in the browser, as runnable code blocks or a persistent interactive terminal – no Redis server needed.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: clear README with many examples and a list of supported commands, Redis mock bundled in dist/index.js. Caveats: only tag 0.0.1 (= HEAD, Oct 2025); commands are written via a JavaScript API (redis.set(...)), not the redis-cli syntax; the header links chartist CSS from jsdelivr at 'latest'.

templates.name: Reference Jump
templates.description: Cross-reference links that switch to another section, scroll to a marked element (sentence, paragraph, formula) and highlight it briefly, so learners find exactly the passage being referred to.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: release 0.0.1 (July 2026), clear README, no external scripts. Narrow purpose: targets must get ids by hand (<span id> or <!-- id="…" -->).

templates.name: SQLite
templates.description: SQLite in the browser via sql.js: executable SQL blocks with HTML table output and a terminal, hidden setup blocks with @SQL.run2, loading .db files from a URL, and EXPORT/IMPORT of databases as files.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: release 0.0.1 equals current main (Aug 2025), README with examples for every macro and the custom EXPORT/IMPORT commands; complements AlaSQL/PGlite/DuckDB when real SQLite files are wanted. The bundled sql.js loads its WebAssembly binary from https://sql.js.org/dist/ (always the latest version, external), which could break the template if sql.js changes; queries run locally in the browser.

templates.name: Tau-Prolog
templates.description: Learners write Prolog programs and run queries against them directly in the course; text quiz answers can be checked with a Prolog goal.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: tag 0.3.0 (2026-02, upgraded to the latest Tau-Prolog), interpreter bundled in js/tau-prolog.min.js so it runs without a CDN, README documents each macro with examples incl. use_module and quiz checking. Narrow subject (logic programming); the README's own import/demo links still point to the master branch.

templates.name: Textmarker
templates.description: Learners highlight text in several colors with a toolbar; marker quizzes check whether the right words were marked in the right color (Check/Solve, optional solution block), pre-highlighted text for demonstrations, and an Explain Word mode that looks up a word in Wiktionary.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: actively maintained (Sep 2026), README with examples, browser test suite; strong value for text work in language and literature lessons. Pinned to a main commit because the README documents features (solution blocks, quiz metadata, Explain Word) that came after the only release 0.0.1. Explain Word sends the selected word to Wikimedia's Wiktionary API (documented in the README); the advanced examples with timer and rewards need the separate lia-timer and lia-loot templates.

templates.name: TikZJax
templates.description: TikZ code is rendered as a vector graphic in the browser, so LaTeX diagrams, geometric figures and technical drawings can be written in the course or edited live by learners.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: released (0.0.1 = current default branch), README with examples for all four macros. dist/index.js loads tikzjax.js and its fonts from tikzjax.com (external host, needs internet); TikZJax supports only part of the LaTeX package world. The README's own versioned import URL contains a stray `blob/` and fails — use the URL here.

templates.name: Virtual Speaker
templates.description: Adds an animated avatar that moves its lips while LiaScript reads narrator comments aloud (text-to-speech or audio recordings); different comments can have different speakers, giving narrated slides a visible presenter.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: maintained (tag 0.1.1, 2026-10), DiceBear bundled locally in dist/index.js (no CDN), extensive README with predefined speakers, styles gallery, settings and JS API; speakers are configured via window.VirtualSpeakerConfig in @onload. Only visible in presentation/slides mode with sound on; requires LiaScript's window.LIA.narrator hook (present in the current master branch, the README still calls it upcoming); avatars of recordings from other domains need CORS to lip-sync.

templates.name: WebSerial
templates.description: Send the code of a LiaScript code block over the Web Serial API to a connected device, e.g. MicroPython on an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi Pico, and read and type into its output in a terminal.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: no external dependencies and tagged (0.0.1, May 2025), but thin docs (one example) and narrow use. Works only in Chrome and Edge (no Firefox/Safari) and needs a device on the learner's computer; baud rate is fixed at 115200 in the macro.

templates.name: Wictionary
templates.description: Words marked in the text become clickable and show their dictionary definition from Wiktionary as a tooltip, in the course language or a language chosen per word — useful for vocabulary work and technical terms.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: released (0.0.2 = current default branch), compact README with examples, no external library. Definitions are fetched live from the Wiktionary API (needs internet; looked-up words go to Wikimedia), and the quality of the definitions depends on the Wiktionary of each language.

templates.name: Wikimedia Commons
templates.description: Embeds images, audio and video from Wikimedia Commons by file name with the correct title, author, licence and source attribution, as single media, a gallery or individual metadata fields.
templates.note: Rating 4/5: maintained (2026, release 0.0.2 identical to main), clear README with examples, and it solves licence attribution for OER. Every view queries commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php and loads the media from Wikimedia servers, so it needs a network connection and learners' browsers contact Wikimedia.

templates.name: A-Frame
templates.description: Embed interactive 3D scenes written in A-Frame HTML, 3D models (glTF/glb) and 360° panorama images that learners can rotate and explore directly on a slide.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: versioned (0.0.6) with a README that documents every macro with examples; useful for 3D/VR-style visualisations. Unmaintained since 2021; each scene is an iframe that loads A-Frame 1.2.0 from aframe.io plus aframe-extras/orbit-controls from unpkg (all reachable when checked), so it needs internet and uses an old A-Frame release. @AFRAME.style is the overridable default style, not a block macro.

templates.name: AlaSQL
templates.description: Executable SQL blocks run by the in-browser AlaSQL database; tables can be filled from CSV data.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: simple and light, but unmaintained since 2020, no release (pinned to a commit) and an old AlaSQL 0.6.5 from a CDN; AlaSQL's SQL dialect differs from real databases. For standard SQL prefer PGlite or DuckDB.

templates.name: Annotation Overlay
templates.description: Adds a toolbar to every slide so teachers (or learners) can draw freehand annotations with pen and eraser, undo/redo and hide them during a live presentation; optionally recognises handwritten answers (OCR) and turns axis sketches into coordinate systems.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: UI plugin without macros (import only; control via window.__LIA_ANNOTATION__), README documents toolbar, options panels and JS API. Pinned to commit: main is 14 commits ahead of tag 0.0.1 (OCR, coordinate widgets, scroller fixes). That header imports lia-canvas-ocr, JSXGraph and lia-coordinate from their unpinned main branches; lia-canvas-ocr loads transformers.js/ML models and KaTeX from jsDelivr/esm.sh and calls a translation API, so it is heavy, needs internet and is not fully reproducible. Tag 0.0.1 is a lean pen/eraser-only alternative.

templates.name: BiwaScheme
templates.description: Editable Scheme code blocks run in the browser by the BiwaScheme interpreter, optionally followed by an interactive terminal (REPL) for further experiments.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: works and runs fully client-side, but the README is short, Scheme is a niche teaching language and there is no release. Pinned to commit 8556dd2 (no tags); loads BiwaScheme 0.8.0 from www.biwascheme.org (a local copy lies in the repo but the header does not use it).

templates.name: ChemfigJS
templates.description: Draws chemical structural formulas as SVG from a chemfig-like code (single/double/triple bonds, rings, branches, charges, lone pairs, colors), directly in the course text.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: small self-contained script without external CDNs, useful companion to ChemmacrosJS for structural formulas. Pinned to a commit (no release tag); the author marks it as under development (no fused rings yet, only a workaround). The README documents the chemfig syntax but shows no LiaScript call — from the header, the formula code is the macro parameter, e.g. @chemfig(*6(-=-=-=)); the demo therefore renders no formula. On a syntax error the error alert itself fails (references a variable before it is declared).

templates.name: CodeRunner
templates.description: Makes code blocks in more than 60 compiled and interpreted languages (C, C++, Java, Rust, Go, Haskell, R, Prolog, VHDL, …) executable, optionally with an interactive shell (_withShell) after the run.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: actively maintained, broad and well documented, with a one-line macro per language. Pinned to commit d41b666 because the only tag (0.0.3) is 106 commits behind; all code is sent over WebSocket to an external server (wss://ancient-hollows-41316.herokuapp.com), so it needs internet, depends on that server staying up and should not be used with personal data. The README mentions @LIA.delphi, but the header does not define it (use @LIA.eval with fpc instead).

templates.name: dbdiagram
templates.description: Turns DBML code blocks into interactive entity-relationship diagrams embedded from dbdiagram.io, as a fixed diagram, an editable block, or an executable block learners can change and re-render.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: release 0.0.1 with a clear README including a DBML syntax guide. Every diagram is rendered in an iframe by the external commercial service dbdiagram.io (the schema is sent in the URL), so it needs internet access and stops working if that embed endpoint changes.

templates.name: Drag and Drop Quizzes
templates.description: Drag-and-drop exercises: put items into the correct order, or drag the correct items from a pool into a selection, with instant ✅/❌ feedback.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: easy to use (items separated by |, @uid as first parameter), useful for ordering tasks. Single upload from Jan 2025, pinned to a commit (no release); loads SortableJS 1.14.0 from cdnjs. Answers are neither stored nor counted in LiaScript's quiz evaluation, feedback is only an emoji, and the labels "Pool:" / "Your Selection:" are fixed in English.

templates.name: DynFlex
templates.description: Side-by-side content cards that learners can resize by dragging, with configurable columns and widths; quiz fields inside the cards each get their own check button, e.g. for worksheet-style layouts.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: well documented and actively maintained, but a pure layout aid with no macros — authors use the CSS classes `dynFlex` (container, with data-columns, data-widths, data-store …) and `flex-child`. Pinned to commit 7e0b6f8 (pushed 2026-10-30), because the only tag 0.0.1 lacks most documented features; the README cites a version 1.0.4 for which no tag exists, so its pinned import and jsDelivr URLs fail.

templates.name: ExplainGit
templates.description: An interactive git playground: learners type git commands and see the commit graph with branches and HEAD update live; a code block can preconfigure the repository with a sequence of commands.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: clear teaching value for git basics, but last changed 2020 and the README itself warns that branches on the remote origin are not supported. Pinned to commit 235ff5c (no tags); the playground loads D3 v5 from d3js.org and the repo's bundle.min.js/explaingit.min.css from jsDelivr without a version, i.e. always the current default branch.

templates.name: Fullscreen
templates.description: Hides the LiaScript navigation bar while the course is in browser fullscreen (F11), so slides use the whole screen in presentations; it works automatically after the import.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: small plugin without macros (only an @onload script), unchanged since 2022 (release 0.0.1). It overwrites window.onresize and relies on LiaScript's internal element id lia-toolbar-nav (still present in the current LiaScript source), so it may clash with other scripts or break with future LiaScript versions.

templates.name: G-Code Preview
templates.description: Visualises G-code for CNC machines and 3D printers as an interactive 3D toolpath preview, either static or as an editable, animated code block, and can load large .gcode files by link.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: works self-contained (gcode-preview bundled in dist/index.js) and has a single tagged release 0.0.1 (main only adds a LICENSE since), but it is niche and the README's import lines wrongly point to the ABCjs template; use the import URL above.

templates.name: GGBScript
templates.description: Geometric constructions written as short GeoGebra-like commands in German (Punkt, Gerade, Strecke, Vektor, Kreis, Ellipse, Vieleck, Schnittpunkt, Winkel, Lot …) and drawn as an editable figure in the course.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: many worked examples in the README, runs without external services (drawn with LiaScript's built-in chart component, not GeoGebra itself). The README states it is an experimental, incomplete version created with ChatGPT; command names and README are German only. Pinned to a commit (no release), last change Feb 2025.

templates.name: JSCAD
templates.description: Learners write JavaScript code that builds 3D models (e.g. cubes and spheres) and see the result in an interactive 3D viewer next to the code; good for parametric design and spatial geometry.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: useful for parametric 3D design, but rendering happens in an iframe of the external service jscad.app (code passed gzip-compressed in the URL fragment), so it needs that site online. Tag 0.0.1 (= HEAD, April 2025), short README, no license file; pako loaded from cdnjs.

templates.name: JSCPP
templates.description: Makes C++ code blocks editable and runnable in the browser with the JSCPP interpreter, optionally with a second block as standard input; errors are marked in the editor.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: simple and server-free, but unmaintained since 2019 and pinned to a commit (no release tag). Loads JSCPP unversioned from felixhao28.github.io (reachable at check time); JSCPP is an interpreter for a subset of C++, so templates, much of the STL and modern C++ features may not run.

templates.name: KekuleJS
templates.description: Renders molecules from CML, MOL and other chemistry formats as 2D drawings or rotatable 3D models, loads molecule files, and adds an interactive periodic table.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: strong for chemistry lessons with working examples, but no releases and last changed in 2023; the header also defines undocumented 2D variants @Kekule.load2d and @Kekule.eval2d. Pinned to commit (no tags); kekule.min.js, three.js and the CSS load unpinned from cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/LiaTemplates/KekuleJS (latest default branch), and raphael is requested via plain http from cdnjs, which browsers block as mixed content; CML input must not contain @ characters.

templates.name: LiaScript Freeze
templates.description: Learners freeze their quiz answers into a submission link; the teacher opens it locked for review with automatic scoring, point corrections and a PDF report, plus an optional timed exam mode.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: strong assessment use without a server (answers travel in the link) and a very detailed README, but no releases, no licence file, and changes almost daily (version 1.0.2 in the header); macro names are German, the interface follows the course language (de/en). Pinned to commit (no tags); its header imports JSXGraph@main and seven MINT-the-GAP templates from moving branches (main, one from a Proposal branch), and the optional F12/Tab/Time tracking should be discussed with learners before use.

templates.name: LogicEmu
templates.description: Draw logic circuits (switches, gates, LEDs, adders) as ASCII diagrams in a code block and let learners run or edit the live simulation of the LogicEmu emulator.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: two simple macros, short README with a working example each; good for digital-logic lessons. Pinned to commit (no tag, last change 2019); the simulation runs in an iframe from liatemplates.github.io/LogicEmu/docs (reachable when checked), which follows the repository's master branch and is not pinned; LogicEmu's ASCII circuit syntax must be learned from the upstream LogicEmu project.

templates.name: mec2
templates.description: Renders interactive 2D physics/mechanism simulations (nodes, masses, constraints, gravity, e.g. pendulums and linkages) from a JSON model, either as a fixed simulation or as an editable block learners can modify and rerun.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: strong visual demos, but unmaintained since 2020, pinned to a commit (no release tag), and the README only shows examples without explaining the mec2 JSON model (see goessner.github.io/mec2). Loads its scripts unversioned from a third-party GitHub Pages site (jauhl.github.io/mecEdit, reachable at check time), so upstream changes can break it.

templates.name: Navigation
templates.description: Replaces the default table of contents with a collapsible, hierarchical navigation tree with bookmarks, active-slide highlighting and remembered state – helpful for long courses with many sections.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: works by import alone – it defines no macros, so the macro list is empty. Tag 0.0.2 (= HEAD, Oct 2026), actively developed; the README is very short (no screenshots or options), no license file, and it changes LiaScript's UI, so test it with your course.

templates.name: Pannellum
templates.description: Shows 360° panorama images (equirectangular) and 360° videos that learners can look around in, optionally with info hotspots — e.g. for virtual field trips or museum visits.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: simple, documented macros with live examples; @Pannellum.hotspots is an authoring helper that logs click positions to the console. Unmaintained since 2019, pinned to a commit (no release). Loads Pannellum 2.4 and video.js 7.1 from cdn.pannellum.org, pannellum.org and vjs.zencdn.net (checked reachable 2026-10-30), including the pannellum.org website stylesheet; panorama images must be served with CORS.

templates.name: Periodic Table
templates.description: Embeds an interactive periodic table of the elements on a slide, where learners can look up element data while working.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: does one thing (an embedded periodic table based on Bowserinator's Periodic-Table-JSON, CC BY-SA) with two macros; very thin README, header still has template placeholders (author 'Your Name') and the README's own import line points to a github.com/blob URL instead of raw. Pinned to commit (no tag, last change 2021); the table is an iframe from liatemplates.github.io/PeriodicTable (self-contained page, reachable when checked) that follows the main branch.

templates.name: ProcessingJS
templates.description: Editable Processing sketches (creative coding: drawings, animations, simple simulations) run on a canvas directly below the code block.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: one simple macro with several demo sketches in the README, but last changed 2020 and based on Processing.js 1.6.6 (loaded from cdnjs), a library no longer developed. Pinned to commit f17c3e6 (no tags); only one sketch runs at a time.

templates.name: PyScript
templates.description: Turns Python code blocks into editable PyScript REPLs that run in the browser, with optional preloading of packages such as numpy and matplotlib for plots.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: versioned (0.0.4, identical to main) with clear examples, but frozen on an early 2022 PyScript alpha (py-env, py-repl) and not maintained since; the Pyodide template is the more current choice for Python. Loads its bundle from cdn.jsdelivr.net (pinned @0.0.4) and Pyodide v0.20.0 from cdn.jsdelivr.net (large download); the course needs persistent: true in its header.

templates.name: Qalb (قلب)
templates.description: Executes code blocks in Qalb, a small Lisp/Scheme-like language written entirely in Arabic script and Arabic-Indic numerals, directly in the browser – programming in the learners' own script.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: runs offline in the browser (interpreter bundled in dist/index.js) and the README is a complete interactive tutorial, but it is written only in Arabic and right-to-left code blocks need <!-- data-rtl -->. No release yet, pinned to commit 5688cda (July 2026).

templates.name: Random
templates.description: Simple quiz banks: wrap quizzes (or any content) in elements with class "random" and show only a given number of them at random, optionally weighted and limited to quizzes not yet solved.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: useful for varied practice, README explains both macros with examples and no external scripts are loaded. Last change 2020, pinned to a commit (no release); a fork of fjangfaragesh/liaRandomSelector with own later changes. The selection works per slide via HTML divs; the "only unsolved" filter relies on LiaScript's internal quiz class name "open" (still present in current LiaScript sources); @Random.static keeps its selection only until the page is reloaded. The README's own import line uses a github.com URL — use the raw import below.

templates.name: Speech Recognition Quiz
templates.description: Pronunciation quizzes: learners say a given phrase in a chosen language and the browser's speech recognition checks it, optionally showing what it understood on a mismatch.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: clear README with examples in several languages and a release (0.0.1, identical to main), no external libraries. Works only where the Web Speech API exists (per README Chrome, Edge, Opera; not Firefox or Safari), and contrary to the README's 'no server calls' Chrome sends the recorded audio to Google's speech service, a privacy point for schools; needs microphone permission.

templates.name: SpreadSheet
templates.description: Embeds editable, Excel-like spreadsheets (formulas such as =SUM, dropdown, checkbox and calendar columns, sorting, several worksheets) configured as JSON, so learners can calculate and explore data inside the course.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: one tagged release (0.0.1, 2025) and a README with good examples, but JSpreadsheet CE and jSuites are loaded from the vendor's own servers under a floating 'v5' path, so updates or outages there can break it. Entries are lost when the slide is left unless the slide sets persistent: true; nothing is graded.

templates.name: TextAnalysis
templates.description: Gives instant feedback on texts learners write into an editable block: word, syllable and sentence counts, readability scores (Flesch, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Dale-Chall, …) and estimated reading and speaking time.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: release 0.0.1, unchanged since 2021; README explains each metric. Based on the npm package text-readability, whose formulas and word lists are designed for English, so scores for German or other languages are not meaningful. Lowercase metric names return values only, uppercase ones add explanations; script loaded from jsDelivr pinned to 0.0.1.

templates.name: TinyTurtle
templates.description: Turtle graphics in plain JavaScript: learners steer a turtle with forward, left, right and pen commands on a canvas of chosen size, optionally typing commands live in a console.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: simple, beginner-friendly and documented (methods listed in the README), but unchanged since 2020 and without release, so pinned to commit 0f3ab29. The header loads tiny-turtle.js from jsDelivr's unpinned branch URL, so the import pin does not fix the library itself; the README's own import line is not a raw URL – use the one above.

templates.name: Vega
templates.description: Declarative data visualizations with Vega-Lite: write a JSON chart specification (data inline or from a URL) and show it as a chart, optionally as an editable code block learners can change and re-run.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: short README with examples, more chart types than LiaScript's built-in charts. Unmaintained since 2020, pinned to a commit (no release); loads vega 5.9.0, vega-lite 4.0.2 and vega-embed 6.2.1 from jsDelivr (reachable 2026-10-30) — specs written for the current Vega-Lite 5 docs may not all work.

templates.name: VTK
templates.description: Write and run vtk.js code for scientific 3D visualization, or load volume data sets (e.g. a CT head scan) into an interactive volume viewer.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: works for advanced users, but script https://unpkg.com/vtk.js is unpinned (currently 38.x) and may break with future releases; @VTK.load and @VTK.loadIframe use data and a viewer on kitware.github.io / data.kitware.com. Pinned to commit (no tag, last change 2020); short README.

templates.name: WebDev
templates.description: Makes HTML, JavaScript, HTML+CSS and HTML+JavaScript code blocks editable and runnable, rendering the result right below so learners can experiment with front-end basics.
templates.note: Rating 3/5: minimal and server-free, but unmaintained since 2019 and pinned to a commit (no release tag). HTML and JavaScript run directly in the course page (only @WebDev.HTML_CSS uses an iframe), so learner code can interfere with the page.
